tendencies.text: Rank candidates who have led rounds (role lead, high lead_share) above those who only joined rounds; a candidate seen only as a participant goes in rejected with reason follower_only when lead history is known.
Reject only on an observed fact: stage, sector, country or check size that clearly does not fit the subject. A missing or unknown field never rejects; rank it lower and say confidence low.
Prefer candidates with a lead in the 24 months before request.as_of; mark older activity as inactive. Ignore anything dated after request.as_of.
Every reason cites at least one evidence id from the evidence list; add each profile fact or web page you rely on to evidence once, with its ref or url.
Use only candidate ids from the input, each at most once across matches and rejected; never add the subject or new names.

Before scoring, drop every fact dated after request.as_of, including last_lead_date. For example, a 2023-06-01 Mistral fact cannot be used when as_of is 2023-05-31. Add a warning for each dropped fact so no later knowledge leaks into the ranking.

Rank on lead behaviour first. A dated 'Led X' fact at the subject's stage in the 12-18 months before as_of is the strongest signal: set role=lead, fill last_lead_date and mark it active. 'Invested in' facts only support role=participant. Reject as follower_only only when the evidence shows the candidate follows and never leads.

Use separate score_parts for stage, sector, geography, check size compared with raising.amount (leads write 50-70% of a round), lead record and recency. Judge sector fit from recent deals, not the fund's name. Reject for stage, size or sector mismatch only when the evidence clearly rules the candidate out.

When a candidate has no facts, do not invent a history. Give it role=unknown, status 'unknown', low confidence and a score below candidates with evidence. Do not reject it as inactive without proof. Use only web pages dated on or before as_of, and cite each with its url and date.

Return at most top_k matches, using only the given ids, ordered by score. Every reason must cite real evidence ids. Set confidence to high only when a dated lead fact matches the subject's stage, sector and region. Treat a fact shared by many candidates as weak evidence and add a warning.

notes: Drafted by the training research step from web search. Not validated.
